data: synthetic test days 42-59, frozen model hgb-86it-677lab-nocallerid, policy v4

groups.title: One small payment (under ₹10,000) and nothing else on file
groups.explanation: The whole scam was a single small payment. With no history building up and no flag on the payee, there is almost nothing to separate it from the many genuine first payments of that size.

reasons_it_would_show.en: First payment to this account, 10x your usual payment

This account had no activity for 6 months before today

groups.title: One larger payment to a payee with no outside flag
groups.explanation: A single larger payment to an account that had never been reported and was not in a detected mule network. Without a second payment, the journey signals (rising amounts, several new payees) never appear, and the payee family has nothing to go on.

reasons_it_would_show.en: First payment to this account, 760x your usual payment
This account had no activity for 27 months before today

groups.title: A short run of small payments (all under ₹10,000), payee never flagged
groups.explanation: Two to five small payments, often 'fees' or 'test' amounts, to clean-looking accounts. Each one is small enough to look like everyday spending, and the run ended before the series features or the mule-network detector caught up. Loan-fee and marketplace scams make up most of this group.

groups.title: Several larger payments that stayed just under the pause line, payee never flagged
groups.explanation: Several larger payments, but each step stayed just under the pause line: the payee was never flagged and the growth from one payment to the next was gradual. The memory rule only escalates after a warning, so it never started.

way_out.text: 76 of the 82 were a pause: the customer sees three facts, waits 30 seconds and can press Continue, so the cost is about half a minute. 6 reached a trusted check (₹50,000+ with two kinds of evidence, or within 7 days of continuing past a warning): the payment waits for the trusted person or up to an hour, then the customer decides. 0 reached a hold, so no genuine payment was stopped for an officer.

round1.measured: 82% of victims warned, 35% at the first payment, 76% when the type is hidden from training (n = 34)
round1.why: small amounts to clean accounts, often without a call; the 'pay to receive' QR trick is not modelled

round1.what: All three scammer tactics at once (no calls, clean mules, no hooks)
round1.why: each tactic silences one kind of evidence; together they leave mostly the journey family

round1.what: Scam-type guesser on the new loan-fee scam
round1.measured: right 0.3% of the time when it names a type (it names one for 72% of warned loan-fee payments)
round1.why: it had only 2 loan-fee labels, so it confidently names a known type instead of saying 'unfamiliar'; officers would see a wrong label exactly when a new scam appears. It never changes the tier or the advice the customer sees
